text_post: Just like it's not only women who believe in Women Firstism, it does not follow political division lines, either.  People tend to look out for Number One no matter who they are or where and when they live. In the gender binary (there, I said it), as it includes differences of interest, men and women become like different "tribes", or competitors.  Even if one looks back to before 20th century feminism, or before the birth of medieval romantic love (which IMO is not quite the same as chivalry), there are few examples of societies where love does not come at a price for men. Of course it came at a price for women, too; the actual arrangements come down to bargaining for benefits. If that's so, there has always been a Women First movement among women; we find it today in the "traditional" women's role, which includes at least as much privilege as it includes "submission". In that sense, Women Firstism is just as important for conservatives; it's just that conservatives have no -ism - the whole point of being conservative is keeping things about the same as they are (except for some who want it to be even more so), which makes sense if the system as it is serves your interests. (The -isms are reserved for the have-nots. -Isms are a map and an action plan and is something you need to coordinate people, which you need to build up a large enough group, which you need to have as much power as those which have economic and political power.) Two very important things happened between  the years1900 and 2000: Affluence and The Pill.  The first one actually took 100 years, but the West has passed a tipping point where the good life is no longer dependent on getting stuff at all, but merely selecting the right stuff. Material wealth abounds and can be had for comparatively little effort: a little education and a littel work, and life is better than it ever was for 99% of all our forefathers. That makes the role of provider obsolete, and this has decreased women's dependency on men, increasing their power; while it has increased men's dependency on women's good will, and decreased their power. The Pill arrived in a single year - 1965? - but it will be a long time before its final effects have all become evident. I think we vastly underestimate the impact of this little pharmaceutical device on the human race and human society. For aeons, biology, for women, had meant destiny - but no longer. Contraception separated sex from marriage - and marriage was when a man took over the role of provider. So contraception has made the husband obsolete, too, and this has decreased women's dependency on men, increasing their power; while it has increased men's dependency on women's good will, and decreased their power. Legislating parenthood has also transferred ownership of children from the father to the mother, again making an old mens' role - fatherhood - dependent on the good will of women, i.e. obsolete, again decreasing women's dependency on men, increasing their power; while increasing men's dependency on women's good will, and decreasing their power. So, overall, the century which saw millions of men persecuted, imprisoned, displaced, maimed, crippled, tortured and killed - and the ones not victims of tyranny and war building modern society - , has rewarded them with being made obsolete, reducing their social status, increasing their dependency on women, while women have had their independency reduced and their power increased. And while mens' power always implicitly and explicitly included responsibilities and duties, no such responsibilities and duties have been shifted towards women. In the few areas where the change has left women with the bill - e.g. single mothers - the situation is deplored (and blamed on men - i.e. the responsibilities remain). In so many ways, this is no longer a man's world. Feminism as part of Women Firstism is the official Trade Union front conducting the concerted effort by women of the - traditionally conservative - upper and - traditionally bourgeois - middle class, to achieve resource transfer just for being women, from social and legal rights and entitlements, to countless jobs directly related to feminism in academia and public offices, to white collar jobs in tertiary and qarternary industries (services, media, etc.) generated by selling their vote to the highest bidder (in the USA, traditonally the Democrats). Cats, too, expect to be fed just for being cats; and if they choose to chase the odd mouse, it is because even cats deserve some light diversion  from time to time. Now, it only stands to reason that people, even privileged people, engaged in hogging wealth should appropriate the rethoric of the underprivileged, like the labour movement, the civil rights movement and perhaps even third world liberation movements. Similarly, it stands to reason that they should appropriate some of the effective tactics of social and civil movements. It also stands to reason that this requires an enormous smokescreen. For this reason, feminists, when not gloating over girrrl power, have embroidered on their banner the old narrative from the days when men had more power and more independence. They have invented the non-referring term "patriarchy" for the mechanisms of oppression under which they allegedly suffer; its semantic field corresponds exactly to the downturned thumb from the amphitheatre ranks around the gladiatorial arena: anything they don't like and its your fault. But this smokescreen should not prevent us from seeing that feminism is merely Women First tribalism writ large - the ear-splitting barrage on all sectors on the gender war front, preceding the attack aiming to extend and cement the conquests and concessions in the gender bargaining.  First wave, second wave, third wave and so on feminism climbs the Maslow hierachy. First women secured equal opportunities with men (i.e. in the eyes of the law: the right to education, to work, to vote). Once that power base was secured, they decided that that wasn't really equality: they needed the right to self-realization (no fault divorce, alimony, child support, etc.). As we rise up through the ranks, we get closer and closer to feminine core values: self-realization is not really equality either: now the whole process of reproduction, from how to approach a woman, and what you should wear when doing it, and who shouldn't, to how to flirt and how to court her, where to go on dates and vacations, to the price of the ring and the wedding, and sometimes actually - with more disclaimers than Microsoft  - actual sex, too, is going to be firmly in their hand. The rumblings about self-esteem and body image and trigger words points the way towards the apex: universal princess admiration (unless defrocked by Big Sister).  The only areas where they fail are those few areas where merit is based on merit: where status is linked to creativity, productivity, daring and ingenuity - at the frontlines of science and industry - women have yet to devise a tactic for coming first. In this way, Women Firstism cuts right across all division lines of politics. The very scope of the attack, their inroads into politics and business, their numerical superiority in education, their invasion of the US defence organizations, their slow, but probably invevitable conquest of the Church, it all demonstrates that it is not about left vs. right, but about Women First, whatever the context. Only the label changes; but feminism is not really conservative or liberal or socialist: that would entail that they had to work for and share their achievements with conservative, liberal and socialist men, and they will never do that; they'd rather break a nail.
